# Frozen N9 workloads

`bench/n9/workloads.mjs` derives nine explicitly bounded workloads: three families at 100, 1,000 and 10,000 records. `freeze.json` fixes the complete record, query, membership-judgment, schema and provenance-label SHA-256 identities. Its identities were generated before production searches or timing. The older source snapshot is pinned by its actual file-byte SHA-256 as well as its historical logical corpus hash; current documentation edits do not change these inputs.

- `real-docs` cycles 34 sections from the frozen RX-4001 technical documentation corpus. Each record retains its heading and a whitespace-bounded excerpt of at most 512 UTF-16 code units. These are repeated labeled excerpts, not 10,000 independent real documents.
- `high-cardinality` keeps those excerpts and appends deterministic catalog identifiers, three unique vocabulary terms per record and controlled common/rare/phrase terms. The unique lexical keys distinguish dictionary size from document count.
- `adversarial` retains synthetic text only: common terms, overlapping rare/OR branches, negative-only complements, equality filters, repeated words, and contiguous/gapped/split-value phrase cases. Provenance labels explicitly say no real excerpt is retained.

Each family defines eight cases. The broad synthetic prefix deliberately exceeds the unchanged 256 field/term expansion ceiling, including at 100 records; this is an expected typed refusal rather than an empty success. The narrow synthetic prefix has 30 expansions and ten expected matches. The real-document broad prefix remains within the expansion ceiling, but can still be refused by the execution work/deadline limits at larger sizes. Source phrase rows require the explicitly installed source provider **and** source phrase registration.

Expected full memberships come from direct source predicates using a standalone whole-string Unicode token regex and per-token NFKC/lowercase normalization. The oracle imports no production tokenizer, retrieval code or scorer. Phrase judgments preserve original value boundaries. These are exhaustive lexical membership labels, not relevance judgments, an independently implemented ranking oracle or a representative workload distribution. Production score arithmetic and original-offset qualification remain covered by the separate established tests.

The schema is one `body` text field plus one string `group` metadata field. No runtime cap is raised. Corpus sizes fit the default admission/text/vocabulary ceilings; that admission fact does not promise a query or source restore finishes within work/deadline limits. Build in batches of at most the unchanged native limit of 256 for the normal owner path. Distinct source-package, measured-package and benchmark harness identities belong in the execution report; fixture hashes alone do not establish installed artifact provenance.

Run `node --test test/comparison/n9-workloads.test.mjs` after the normal build. The tests recompute all nine frozen identities and compare complete 100-record memberships against the public runtime, including refusal recovery and phrase value boundaries. The benchmark runner owns larger installed checks and timing. Freeze changes require an intentional version/method review; do not automatically regenerate expected hashes to conceal drift.
